To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the multihead tester scheduling problem can be modeled as a generalized assignment problem, that the problem can be solved by a simple branch and bound algorithm, and that the performance of previously suggested scheduling algorithms is poor.
(1) the multihead tester scheduling problem is a difficult combinatorial problem, and (2) the previously suggested scheduling algorithms are not optimal.

the performance of previously proposed multihead tester scheduling algorithms can be improved by considering the dependency of tester throughput on lot mix, and that an enumeration solution procedure is capable of generating optimal schedules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing scheduling methodologies for the semiconductor device test operations of multi-head testers.
developing a scheduling algorithm which can effectively and efficiently schedule the test operations of a semiconductor device manufacturing firm.
developing a model for the multihead tester scheduling problem and with devising an efficient algorithm that can be used by a semiconductor device test manager to schedule the device test operations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no known scheduling algorithm for multihead testers that is both efficient and optimal.
the scheduling problem for multihead testers is a very difficult one and the solution procedure presented is the only one that is guaranteed to find an optimal solution for the problem.
the problem of scheduling semiconductor device test operations in multihead testers is an NP-complete problem and that previously suggested scheduling methodologies are not adequate for the problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are the first to model the multihead tester scheduling problem accurately and to present an optimal enumeration procedure for it.
a simple heuristic, the first-come first-served (FCFS) policy, performs as well as the best known scheduling algorithm for multihead testers.
the multihead tester scheduling problem has not been solved in the past because it has never been properly defined and modeled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the scheduling of device test operations in semiconductor manufacturing is not an easy task.
the performance of the scheduling algorithms is highly dependent on the lot sizes and the number of lots to be scheduled.
the performance of the scheduling methods depends critically on the number of lots processed simultaneously on the testers.
